title: Au médecin / At the doctor's
bridge: In French, describing symptoms to a doctor requires specific expressions to locate pain and its intensity. Unlike Spanish, you use 'avoir mal à' to say something hurts, and 'depuis' to indicate how long you've had the symptom. The French also expect the doctor to give them an 'ordonnance' (prescription) at the end of the consultation.
rule: Key phrases: 'J'ai mal à...' (I have pain in...), 'Depuis quand?' (Since when?), 'Depuis [time]' (For [time]), 'J'ai de la fièvre' (I have a fever), 'Je me sens mal' (I feel unwell), 'Pouvez-vous me prescrire quelque chose?' (Can you prescribe me something?), 'C'est grave?' (Is it serious?)

concept_examples.text: J'ai mal à la gorge depuis trois jours.
concept_examples.translation: I've had a sore throat for three days.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒe mal a la ɡɔʁʒ dəpɥi tʁwɑ ʒuʁ/

concept_examples.text: Où avez-vous mal exactement?
concept_examples.translation: Where exactly does it hurt?
concept_examples.phonetic: /u ave vu mal ɛɡzaktəmɑ̃/

concept_examples.text: Je vous prescris des antibiotiques.
concept_examples.translation: I'm prescribing you antibiotics.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə vu pʁɛskʁi de zɑ̃tibjɔtik/

common_error.correct_alt: J'ai une douleur à la tête.
common_error.explanation: In French, you don't say 'avoir douleur' directly. The correct construction is 'avoir mal à' for everyday pain, or 'avoir une douleur à' if you want to be more formal or precise. 'Douleur' needs the article 'une'.

examples.original: Bonjour docteur, je ne me sens pas bien.
examples.phonetic: /bɔ̃ʒuʁ dɔktœʁ, ʒə nə mə sɑ̃ pa bjɛ̃/
examples.translation: Hello doctor, I don't feel well.
examples.note: Standard opening phrase in a medical consultation.

examples.original: Qu'est-ce qui vous amène aujourd'hui?
examples.phonetic: /kɛs ki vu zamɛn oʒuʁdɥi/
examples.translation: What brings you here today?
examples.note: Typical doctor's question at the start of the consultation.

examples.original: J'ai mal à la tête et j'ai de la fièvre.
examples.phonetic: /ʒe mal a la tɛt e ʒe də la fjɛvʁ/
examples.translation: I have a headache and a fever.
examples.note: 'Avoir de la fièvre' is the fixed expression for 'to have a fever'.

examples.original: Depuis combien de temps?
examples.phonetic: /dəpɥi kɔ̃bjɛ̃ də tɑ̃/
examples.translation: For how long?
examples.note: The doctor always asks about the duration of the symptom.

examples.original: J'ai une douleur aiguë dans le côté droit depuis hier soir.
examples.phonetic: /ʒe yn dulœʁ eɡy dɑ̃ lə kote dʁwa dəpɥi jɛʁ swaʁ/
examples.translation: I've had a sharp pain in my right side since last night.
examples.note: 'Aigu/aiguë' means sharp (intense, stabbing pain). The gender agrees with 'douleur' (feminine).

examples.original: Est-ce que la douleur est constante ou par moments?
examples.phonetic: /ɛs kə la dulœʁ ɛ kɔ̃stɑ̃t u paʁ mɔmɑ̃/
examples.translation: Is the pain constant or intermittent?
examples.note: The doctor needs to know if it's continuous or intermittent.

examples.original: C'est plutôt par moments, surtout quand je bouge.
examples.phonetic: /sɛ plytot paʁ mɔmɑ̃, syʁtu kɑ̃ ʒə buʒ/
examples.translation: It's more intermittent, especially when I move.
examples.note: 'Surtout quand' means 'especially when'.

examples.original: Je vais vous examiner. Allongez-vous, s'il vous plaît.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə ve vu ɛɡzamine. alɔ̃ʒe vu, sil vu plɛ/
examples.translation: I'm going to examine you. Lie down, please.
examples.note: 'Allongez-vous' is the formal imperative of 's'allonger' (to lie down).

examples.original: D'après vos symptômes, vous avez une infection bactérienne. Je vais vous prescrire des antibiotiques.
examples.phonetic: /dapʁɛ vo sɛ̃ptom, vu zave yn ɛ̃fɛksjɔ̃ baktɛʁjɛn. ʒə ve vu pʁɛskʁiʁ de zɑ̃tibjɔtik/
examples.translation: According to your symptoms, you have a bacterial infection. I'm going to prescribe antibiotics.
examples.note: 'D'après' means 'according to'. 'Prescrire' is the formal verb for 'to prescribe'.

examples.original: Combien de fois par jour dois-je les prendre?
examples.phonetic: /kɔ̃bjɛ̃ də fwa paʁ ʒuʁ dwa ʒə le pʁɑ̃dʁ/
examples.translation: How many times a day should I take them?
examples.note: 'Dois-je' is the formal inversion of 'je dois' (I must). Very common in questions to the doctor.

examples.original: Trois fois par jour, pendant sept jours. Et revenez me voir si ça ne va pas mieux dans 48 heures.
examples.phonetic: /tʁwa fwa paʁ ʒuʁ, pɑ̃dɑ̃ sɛt ʒuʁ. e ʁəvəne mə vwaʁ si sa nə va pa mjø dɑ̃ kaʁɑ̃t ɥit œʁ/
examples.translation: Three times a day for seven days. And come back to see me if you're not better within 48 hours.
examples.note: 'Revenez me voir' is a typical follow-up instruction. '48 heures' is pronounced 'quarante-huit heures'.

examples.original: Est-ce que vous avez une carte Vitale?
examples.phonetic: /ɛs kə vu zave yn kaʁt vital/
examples.translation: Do you have a Vitale card?
examples.note: The carte Vitale is the French health insurance card. It's common to be asked for it when paying.

title: Réserver un hébergement / Booking Accommodation
bridge: When booking accommodation in France, the vocabulary and expectations are similar to the Spanish-speaking world, but there are key phrases you should know. The French are direct when asking about services and conditions. It is important to know how to ask about breakfast ('petit-déjeuner'), wifi, parking, and cancellation conditions before confirming.
rule: Key phrases: 'Je voudrais réserver...' (I would like to book...), 'Avez-vous une chambre disponible?' (Do you have a room available?), 'Pour combien de nuits?' (For how many nights?), 'C'est compris?' (Is it included?), 'Quelles sont les conditions d'annulation?' (What are the cancellation conditions?), 'Y a-t-il le wifi?' (Is there wifi?)

concept_examples.text: Je voudrais réserver une chambre pour deux personnes.
concept_examples.translation: I would like to book a room for two people.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə vudʁɛ ʁezɛʁve yn ʃɑ̃bʁ puʁ dø pɛʁsɔn/

concept_examples.text: Le petit-déjeuner est-il compris dans le prix?
concept_examples.translation: Is breakfast included in the price?
concept_examples.phonetic: /lə pəti deʒœne ɛ til kɔ̃pʁi dɑ̃ lə pʁi/

concept_examples.text: Nous avons une chambre disponible du 15 au 18.
concept_examples.translation: We have a room available from the 15th to the 18th.
concept_examples.phonetic: /nu zavɔ̃ yn ʃɑ̃bʁ dispɔnibl dy kɛ̃z o dizyit/

common_error.wrong: Je veux une chambre pour deux nuits.
common_error.correct: Je voudrais une chambre pour deux nuits.
common_error.correct_alt: Auriez-vous une chambre pour deux nuits?
common_error.explanation: 'Je veux' sounds too abrupt in customer service contexts. In French, it is essential to use the conditional 'je voudrais' (I would like) or ask with 'auriez-vous' to sound polite. Using 'je veux' can be perceived as rude.

examples.original: Bonjour, je voudrais réserver une chambre pour deux nuits, du 20 au 22 juin.
examples.phonetic: /bɔ̃ʒuʁ, ʒə vudʁɛ ʁezɛʁve yn ʃɑ̃bʁ puʁ dø nɥi, dy vɛ̃ o vɛ̃t dø ʒɥɛ̃/
examples.translation: Hello, I would like to book a room for two nights, from June 20 to 22.
examples.note: Always give the check-in and check-out dates from the start.

examples.original: Pour combien de personnes?
examples.phonetic: /puʁ kɔ̃bjɛ̃ də pɛʁsɔn/
examples.translation: For how many people?
examples.note: Standard question before checking availability.

examples.original: Pour deux personnes, s'il vous plaît.
examples.phonetic: /puʁ dø pɛʁsɔn, sil vu plɛ/
examples.translation: For two people, please.
examples.note: Direct and polite response.

examples.original: Oui, nous avons une chambre double disponible. Le prix est de 85 euros par nuit.
examples.phonetic: /wi, nu zavɔ̃ yn ʃɑ̃bʁ dubl dispɔnibl. lə pʁi ɛ də katʁəvɛ̃ sɛ̃k œʁo paʁ nɥi/
examples.translation: Yes, we have a double room available. The price is 85 euros per night.
examples.note: 'Chambre double' can have a double bed or two single beds; it's worth clarifying.

examples.original: Est-ce que le petit-déjeuner est inclus dans ce tarif?
examples.phonetic: /ɛs kə lə pəti deʒœne ɛ ɛ̃kly dɑ̃ sə taʁif/
examples.translation: Is breakfast included in this rate?
examples.note: 'Tarif' is more formal than 'prix' when talking about hotel rates.

examples.original: Non, le petit-déjeuner est en supplément, 12 euros par personne.
examples.phonetic: /nɔ̃, lə pəti deʒœne ɛ tɑ̃ syplemɑ̃, duz œʁo paʁ pɛʁsɔn/
examples.translation: No, breakfast is extra, 12 euros per person.
examples.note: 'En supplément' means 'additional' or 'extra'.

examples.original: Y a-t-il le wifi gratuit dans les chambres?
examples.phonetic: /i a til lə wifi ɡʁatɥi dɑ̃ le ʃɑ̃bʁ/
examples.translation: Is there free wifi in the rooms?
examples.note: 'Wifi' in French is masculine: 'le wifi'. 'Y a-t-il' is the formal interrogative form of 'il y a'.

examples.original: Oui, le wifi est gratuit partout dans l'hôtel. Avez-vous un parking?
examples.phonetic: /wi, lə wifi ɛ ɡʁatɥi paʁtu dɑ̃ lotɛl. ave vu œ̃ paʁkiŋ/
examples.translation: Yes, wifi is free everywhere in the hotel. Do you have parking?
examples.note: 'Partout' means 'everywhere'. 'Parking' is a loanword from English widely used in French.

examples.original: Quelles sont vos conditions d'annulation?
examples.phonetic: /kɛl sɔ̃ vo kɔ̃disjɔ̃ danylɑsjɔ̃/
examples.translation: What are your cancellation conditions?
examples.note: Essential question before providing card details. Policies vary greatly between hotels.

examples.original: Vous pouvez annuler gratuitement jusqu'à 48 heures avant votre arrivée. Au-delà, une nuit vous sera facturée.
examples.phonetic: /vu puve anyle ɡʁatɥitmɑ̃ ʒyska kaʁɑ̃t ɥit œʁ avɑ̃ vɔtʁ aʁive. o dəla, yn nɥi vu səʁa faktyʁe/
examples.translation: You can cancel free of charge up to 48 hours before your arrival. Beyond that, one night will be charged to you.
examples.note: 'Au-delà' means 'beyond' or 'past that limit'. 'Facturer' is the verb 'to charge/invoice'.

examples.original: Parfait. Je confirme la réservation. Pouvez-vous m'envoyer une confirmation par email?
examples.phonetic: /paʁfɛ. ʒə kɔ̃fiʁm la ʁezɛʁvasjɔ̃. puve vu mɑ̃vwaje yn kɔ̃fiʁmasjɔ̃ paʁ iməl/
examples.translation: Perfect. I confirm the reservation. Can you send me a confirmation by email?
examples.note: 'Parfait' is a very useful all-purpose word to express satisfaction. 'Email' or 'courriel' are both valid.

examples.original: Bien sûr. Quelle est votre adresse email? Et à quel nom faut-il faire la réservation?
examples.phonetic: /bjɛ̃ syʁ. kɛl ɛ vɔtʁ adʁɛs iməl? e a kɛl nɔ̃ fo til fɛʁ la ʁezɛʁvasjɔ̃/
examples.translation: Of course. What is your email address? And under what name should the reservation be made?
examples.note: 'À quel nom faut-il faire?' is the standard way to ask for the name for the reservation.

title: À la banque ou bureau de change / At the bank or currency exchange
bridge: In France and French-speaking countries, banking procedures have specific vocabulary. Unlike Spanish, in French you say 'retirer de l'argent' (to withdraw money) and 'effectuer un virement' (to make a transfer). French banks often require supporting documents ('justificatifs') for many operations, and the ATM is called 'distributeur automatique' or simply 'DAB'.
rule: Key phrases: 'Je voudrais ouvrir un compte' (I would like to open an account), 'Je voudrais retirer/déposer de l'argent' (I would like to withdraw/deposit money), 'Quel est le taux de change?' (What is the exchange rate?), 'Il y a des frais?' (Are there fees?), 'Pouvez-vous me donner des billets de...?' (Can you give me bills of...?)

concept_examples.text: Je voudrais changer des dollars en euros.
concept_examples.translation: I would like to exchange dollars for euros.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə vudʁɛ ʃɑ̃ʒe de dɔlaʁ ɑ̃n øʁo/

concept_examples.text: Quel est le taux de change aujourd'hui?
concept_examples.translation: What is the exchange rate today?
concept_examples.phonetic: /kɛl ɛ lə to də ʃɑ̃ʒ oʒuʁdɥi/

concept_examples.text: Y a-t-il des frais de commission?
concept_examples.translation: Are there commission fees?
concept_examples.phonetic: /i a til de fʁɛ də kɔmisjɔ̃/

common_error.correct_alt: Pourriez-vous m'aider à changer de l'argent?
common_error.explanation: Just like at the hotel, using 'je veux' at the bank sounds abrupt. The conditional 'je voudrais' (I would like) is the standard polite form in any formal transaction in France. In banking environments, linguistic politeness is especially important.

examples.original: Bonjour, je voudrais changer 200 dollars américains en euros, s'il vous plaît.
examples.phonetic: /bɔ̃ʒuʁ, ʒə vudʁɛ ʃɑ̃ʒe dø sɑ̃ dɔlaʁ ameʁikɛ̃ ɑ̃n øʁo, sil vu plɛ/
examples.translation: Hello, I would like to exchange 200 US dollars into euros, please.
examples.note: Always specify the source currency ('dollars américains', 'livres sterling', 'pesos mexicains', etc.).

examples.original: Bien sûr. Le taux de change actuel est de 1 dollar pour 0,92 euro.
examples.phonetic: /bjɛ̃ syʁ. lə to də ʃɑ̃ʒ aktɥɛl ɛ də œ̃ dɔlaʁ puʁ zeʁo viŋt dø øʁo/
examples.translation: Of course. The current exchange rate is 1 dollar for 0.92 euros.
examples.note: 'Actuel' means 'current/prevailing', not 'actual' in the temporal sense, which can be confusing due to the false friend.

examples.original: Est-ce qu'il y a des frais?
examples.phonetic: /ɛs kil i a de fʁɛ/
examples.translation: Are there fees?
examples.note: 'Frais' (plural) means fees, charges, or costs. 'Frais de change' are specifically exchange fees.

examples.original: Oui, nous prenons une commission de 2%. Cela vous convient?
examples.phonetic: /wi, nu pʁənɔ̃ yn kɔmisjɔ̃ də dø puʁsɑ̃. səla vu kɔ̃vjɛ̃/
examples.translation: Yes, we charge a 2% commission. Does that work for you?
examples.note: 'Cela vous convient?' is a very French way to ask for confirmation before proceeding.

examples.original: Je voudrais retirer 300 euros de mon compte, s'il vous plaît.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə vudʁɛ ʁətiʁe tʁwa sɑ̃ øʁo də mɔ̃ kɔ̃t, sil vu plɛ/
examples.translation: I would like to withdraw 300 euros from my account, please.
examples.note: 'Retirer' is the verb for withdrawing money. 'Compte' is the bank account.

examples.original: Pouvez-vous me présenter votre carte bancaire et une pièce d'identité?
examples.phonetic: /puve vu mə pʁezɑ̃te vɔtʁ kaʁt bɑ̃kɛʁ e yn pjɛs didɑ̃tite/
examples.translation: Can you present your bank card and an ID document?
examples.note: 'Pièce d'identité' is the generic term for any identification document (passport, ID card, etc.).

examples.original: Voilà ma carte et mon passeport.
examples.phonetic: /vwala ma kaʁt e mɔ̃ paspɔʁ/
examples.translation: Here are my card and my passport.
examples.note: 'Voilà' is used to present or hand over something physically, like 'here you go' or 'here is'.

examples.original: Comment souhaitez-vous les billets? En coupures de 50 ou de 20?
examples.phonetic: /kɔmɑ̃ swɛte vu le bijɛ? ɑ̃ kupyʁ də sɛ̃kɑ̃t u də vɛ̃/
examples.translation: How would you like the bills? In denominations of 50 or 20?
examples.note: 'Coupure' means bill denomination. 'Souhaitez-vous' is the polite form of 'do you wish?'.

examples.original: Je viens d'arriver en France et je voudrais ouvrir un compte bancaire. Quels documents faut-il fournir?
examples.phonetic: /ʒə vjɛ̃ daʁive ɑ̃ fʁɑ̃s e ʒə vudʁɛ uvʁiʁ œ̃ kɔ̃t bɑ̃kɛʁ. kɛl dɔkymɑ̃ fo til fuʁniʁ/
examples.translation: I have just arrived in France and I would like to open a bank account. What documents are required?
examples.note: 'Je viens de + infinitive' expresses 'to have just done something'. 'Fournir' means to provide or supply documents.

examples.original: Il vous faut une pièce d'identité, un justificatif de domicile et un justificatif de revenus.
examples.phonetic: /il vu fo yn pjɛs didɑ̃tite, œ̃ ʒystifikatif də dɔmisil e œ̃ ʒystifikatif də ʁəvəny/
examples.translation: You need an ID document, proof of address, and proof of income.
examples.note: 'Justificatif' is the key word for all documents that prove something in France. 'De domicile' proves your address.

examples.original: Je voudrais aussi effectuer un virement vers l'Espagne. Est-ce possible depuis votre agence?
examples.phonetic: /ʒə vudʁɛ osi ɛfɛktɥe œ̃ viʁmɑ̃ vɛʁ lɛspaɲ. ɛs kə posibl dəpɥi vɔtʁ aʒɑ̃s/
examples.translation: I would also like to make a transfer to Spain. Is it possible from your branch?
examples.note: 'Effectuer un virement' is the formal expression for making a bank transfer. 'Agence' is the bank branch.

examples.original: Oui, tout à fait. Pour un virement SEPA vers l'Espagne, les délais sont de un à deux jours ouvrés.
examples.phonetic: /wi, tu ta fɛ. puʁ œ̃ viʁmɑ̃ sepa vɛʁ lɛspaɲ, le delɛ sɔ̃ də œ̃ a dø ʒuʁ uvʁe/
examples.translation: Yes, absolutely. For a SEPA transfer to Spain, the processing time is one to two business days.
examples.note: 'Tout à fait' is a very French emphatic affirmation. 'Jours ouvrés' are business days (working days, excluding weekends and holidays).

phonetic: /a la bɑ̃k u byʁo də ʃɑ̃ʒ/

translations.en: At the bank or currency exchange

title: Entretien d'embauche basique / Basic job interview
bridge: In France, a job interview has its own rituals: the handshake is mandatory, using 'tu' with the interviewer would be a serious mistake, and the candidate is expected to present their 'parcours' (career path) concisely. Unlike Spanish, in French you say 'postuler à un poste' (to apply for a position) and 'CV' (resume) is pronounced in French. Knowing how to talk about availability and motivation with simple sentences is key at this A2 level.
rule: Key phrases: 'Je me présente...' (I introduce myself...), 'J'ai [X] ans d'expérience' (I have [X] years of experience), 'Je suis disponible à partir du...' (I am available from...), 'Pourquoi avez-vous postulé?' (Why did you apply?), 'Quelles sont vos compétences?' (What are your skills?), 'Je travaille actuellement chez...' (I currently work at...)

concept_examples.text: Je me présente: je m'appelle Laura Díaz, j'ai 28 ans.
concept_examples.translation: I introduce myself: my name is Laura Díaz, I am 28 years old.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə mə pʁezɑ̃t: ʒə mapɛl loʁa djaz, ʒe vɛ̃t ɥit ɑ̃/

concept_examples.text: J'ai deux ans d'expérience dans la vente.
concept_examples.translation: I have two years of experience in sales.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒe dø zɑ̃ dɛkspɛʁjɑ̃s dɑ̃ la vɑ̃t/

concept_examples.text: Je suis disponible immédiatement.
concept_examples.translation: I am available immediately.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə sɥi dispɔnibl imedjatmlɑ̃/

common_error.wrong: Je suis expérimenté dans les ventes.
common_error.correct: J'ai de l'expérience dans la vente.
common_error.correct_alt: J'ai deux ans d'expérience en vente.
common_error.explanation: 'Expérimenté' exists in French but is less natural when talking about oneself in interviews. The most common way is to quantify experience with 'J'ai [X] ans d'expérience dans/en...'. Also, 'les ventes' (plural) is the sector, while 'la vente' (singular) is the activity; both are correct but 'la vente' is more frequent.

levels.label: Se présenter et parler de soi
levels.translation: Introducing yourself and talking about yourself

examples.original: Bonjour, je m'appelle Carlos Romero. Je postule pour le poste de vendeur.
examples.phonetic: /bɔ̃ʒuʁ, ʒə mapɛl kaʁlos ʁomɛʁo. ʒə pɔstyl puʁ lə pɔst də vɑ̃dœʁ/
examples.translation: Hello, my name is Carlos Romero. I am applying for the position of salesperson.
examples.note: 'Postuler pour un poste' is the standard expression for 'to apply for a position'. You do not say 'demander un travail'.

examples.original: Enchanté, Carlos. Pouvez-vous vous présenter en quelques mots?
examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃ʃɑ̃te, kaʁlos. puve vu vu pʁezɑ̃te ɑ̃ kɛlkə mo/
examples.translation: Nice to meet you, Carlos. Can you introduce yourself in a few words?
examples.note: 'En quelques mots' (in a few words) is a very common request at the beginning of the interview.

examples.original: Bien sûr. J'ai 30 ans, je suis espagnol et j'habite à Paris depuis deux ans.
examples.phonetic: /bjɛ̃ syʁ. ʒe tʁɑ̃t ɑ̃, ʒə sɥi ɛspaɲɔl e ʒabit a paʁi dəpɥi dø ɑ̃/
examples.translation: Of course. I am 30 years old, I am Spanish, and I have been living in Paris for two years.
examples.note: 'Depuis' + present indicative to express how long you have been doing something (different from Spanish, which uses the preterite).

examples.original: Très bien. Parlez-moi de votre expérience professionnelle.
examples.phonetic: /tʁɛ bjɛ̃. paʁle mwa də vɔtʁ ɛkspɛʁjɑ̃s pʁɔfɛsjɔnɛl/
examples.translation: Very well. Tell me about your professional experience.
examples.note: 'Parlez-moi de...' is the formal imperative of 'to talk about something'. It is a very common instruction in interviews.

examples.original: J'ai travaillé trois ans comme assistant administratif dans une entreprise de logistique.
examples.phonetic: /ʒe tʁavaje tʁwa zɑ̃ kɔm asistɑ̃ administʁatif dɑ̃z yn ɑ̃tʁəpʁiz də lɔʒistik/
examples.translation: I worked for three years as an administrative assistant in a logistics company.
examples.note: Passé composé to describe specific past experiences with a defined duration.

examples.original: Quelles sont vos principales compétences?
examples.phonetic: /kɛl sɔ̃ vo pʁɛ̃sipal kɔ̃petɑ̃s/
examples.translation: What are your main skills?
examples.note: 'Compétences' is the French word for 'skills' or 'competencies' in the work context.

examples.original: Je suis organisé, je parle espagnol et anglais, et je maîtrise les outils informatiques de base.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə sɥi ɔʁɡanize, ʒə paʁl ɛspaɲɔl e ɑ̃ɡlɛ, e ʒə mɛtʁiz le zutil ɛ̃fɔʁmatik də baz/
examples.translation: I am organized, I speak Spanish and English, and I master basic computer tools.
examples.note: 'Maîtriser' (to master) is the preferred verb for talking about technical skills. 'Outils informatiques' are computer tools.

examples.original: Pourquoi voulez-vous travailler dans notre entreprise?
examples.phonetic: /puʁkwa vule vu tʁavaje dɑ̃ nɔtʁ ɑ̃tʁəpʁiz/
examples.translation: Why do you want to work in our company?
examples.note: Classic motivation question. It is recommended to mention something specific about the company to avoid sounding generic.

examples.original: Parce que votre entreprise a une bonne réputation et je souhaite évoluer dans ce secteur.
examples.phonetic: /paʁs kə vɔtʁ ɑ̃tʁəpʁiz a yn bɔn ʁepytasjɔ̃ e ʒə swɛt evolɥe dɑ̃ sə sɛktœʁ/
examples.translation: Because your company has a good reputation and I wish to grow in this sector.
examples.note: 'Souhaiter + infinitive' (to wish + infinitive) sounds more professional than 'vouloir' in this context.

examples.original: Très bien. Quand seriez-vous disponible pour commencer?
examples.phonetic: /tʁɛ bjɛ̃. kɑ̃ səʁje vu dispɔnibl puʁ kɔmɑ̃se/
examples.translation: Very well. When would you be available to start?
examples.note: 'Seriez-vous' is the conditional of 'être'. The interviewer uses the conditional to be more polite and less direct.

examples.original: Je suis disponible à partir du premier mars. J'ai un préavis d'un mois à respecter.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə sɥi dispɔnibl a paʁtiʁ dy pʁəmje maʁs. ʒe œ̃ pʁeavi dœ̃ mwa a ʁɛspɛkte/
examples.translation: I am available from the first of March. I have a one-month notice period to respect.
examples.note: 'Préavis' is the mandatory notice period before leaving a job. It is a key concept in the French labor system.

examples.original: Est-ce que vous avez des questions pour nous?
examples.phonetic: /ɛs kə vu zave de kɛstjɔ̃ puʁ nu/
examples.translation: Do you have any questions for us?
examples.note: You should always have at least one question prepared. It can be about the team, internal training, or growth prospects.

title: À la poste / At the post office
bridge: The French post office ('La Poste') is much more than a postal service: it also offers banking services ('La Banque Postale') and administrative procedures. When sending packages, the French must choose between different types of delivery: 'lettre prioritaire' (priority letter), 'Colissimo' (national parcel service), or 'recommandé' (certified with proof of receipt). Tracking is done with a tracking number ('numéro de suivi') online.
rule: Key phrases: 'Je voudrais envoyer ce colis' (I would like to send this package), 'En recommandé, s'il vous plaît' (Certified, please), 'Quel est le délai de livraison?' (What is the delivery time?), 'Je voudrais un accusé de réception' (I would like a proof of receipt), 'Où est le guichet?' (Where is the counter?), 'Avez-vous un numéro de suivi?' (Do you have a tracking number?)

concept_examples.text: Je voudrais envoyer ce colis en Espagne.
concept_examples.translation: I would like to send this package to Spain.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə vudʁɛ ɑ̃vwaje sə kɔli ɑ̃n ɛspaɲ/

concept_examples.text: Quel est le délai de livraison en recommandé?
concept_examples.translation: What is the delivery time for certified mail?
concept_examples.phonetic: /kɛl ɛ lə delɛ də livʁɛzɔ̃ ɑ̃ ʁəkɔmɑ̃de/

concept_examples.text: Pouvez-vous me donner le numéro de suivi?
concept_examples.translation: Can you give me the tracking number?
concept_examples.phonetic: /puve vu mə dɔne lə nymeʁo də sɥivi/

common_error.explanation: 'Boîte' means box (the physical object), but in postal services you say 'colis' (package) or 'paquet' to refer to the shipment. Also, 'expédier' is a more formal synonym of 'envoyer' commonly used in postal contexts. As always in services, 'je voudrais' is more polite than 'je veux'.

levels.label: Envoyer une lettre ou un colis
levels.translation: Sending a letter or a package

examples.original: Bonjour, je voudrais envoyer cette lettre en Espagne, s'il vous plaît.
examples.phonetic: /bɔ̃ʒuʁ, ʒə vudʁɛ ɑ̃vwaje sɛt lɛtʁ ɑ̃n ɛspaɲ, sil vu plɛ/
examples.translation: Hello, I would like to send this letter to Spain, please.
examples.note: 'Cette lettre' (this letter) — the demonstrative 'cette' is used with feminine singular nouns.

examples.original: En lettre ordinaire ou en recommandé?
examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃ lɛtʁ ɔʁdinɛʁ u ɑ̃ ʁəkɔmɑ̃de/
examples.translation: By regular mail or certified?
examples.note: 'Recommandé' is certified mail, with a tracking number and recipient's signature. It always costs more.

examples.original: En recommandé, s'il vous plaît. C'est un document important.
examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃ ʁəkɔmɑ̃de, sil vu plɛ. sɛ tœ̃ dɔkymɑ̃ ɛ̃pɔʁtɑ̃/
examples.translation: Certified, please. It's an important document.
examples.note: Justifying the choice of delivery type is optional but natural in conversation.

examples.original: D'accord. Posez-la sur la balance, s'il vous plaît.
examples.phonetic: /dakɔʁ. poze la syʁ la balɑ̃s, sil vu plɛ/
examples.translation: Okay. Put it on the scale, please.
examples.note: 'Balance' (scale) is the instrument for weighing shipments. 'Posez' is the imperative of 'poser' (to place).

examples.original: Ce colis pèse 2 kilos. Vous préférez Colissimo ou Chronopost?
examples.phonetic: /sə kɔli pɛz dø kilo. vu pʁefɛʁe kɔlisimo u kʁɔnopɔst/
examples.translation: This package weighs 2 kilos. Do you prefer Colissimo or Chronopost?
examples.note: Colissimo is La Poste's standard service (2-3 days). Chronopost is the express service (24h) but much more expensive.

examples.original: Quelle est la différence de prix?
examples.phonetic: /kɛl ɛ la difɛʁɑ̃s də pʁi/
examples.translation: What is the price difference?
examples.note: Direct and very useful question. 'La différence de prix' between two options.

examples.original: Colissimo coûte 12 euros avec livraison en 3 jours. Chronopost coûte 22 euros pour le lendemain avant midi.
examples.phonetic: /kɔlisimo kut duz øʁo avɛk livʁɛzɔ̃ ɑ̃ tʁwa ʒuʁ. kʁɔnopɔst kut vɛ̃t dø øʁo puʁ lə lɑ̃dmɛ̃ avɑ̃ midi/
examples.translation: Colissimo costs 12 euros with delivery in 3 days. Chronopost costs 22 euros for the next day before noon.
examples.note: 'Avant midi' (before noon) is a common time specification for urgent deliveries.

examples.original: Je prends Colissimo alors. Est-ce qu'il y a un suivi en ligne?
examples.phonetic: /ʒə pʁɑ̃ kɔlisimo alɔʁ. ɛs kil i a œ̃ sɥivi ɑ̃ liɲ/
examples.translation: Then I'll take Colissimo. Is there online tracking?
examples.note: 'Suivi en ligne' is package tracking on the internet. 'Alors' means 'then' as a decision connector.

examples.original: Bonjour, j'attends un colis depuis une semaine mais il n'est toujours pas arrivé.
examples.phonetic: /bɔ̃ʒuʁ, ʒatɑ̃ œ̃ kɔli dəpɥi yn səmɛn mɛ il nɛ tuʒuʁ pa aʁive/
examples.translation: Hello, I've been waiting for a package for a week but it still hasn't arrived.
examples.note: 'Il n'est toujours pas arrivé' — 'toujours pas' means 'still not' (persistent negation over time).

examples.original: Avez-vous le numéro de suivi? Je vais vérifier pour vous.
examples.phonetic: /ave vu lə nymeʁo də sɥivi? ʒə ve veʁifje puʁ vu/
examples.translation: Do you have the tracking number? I'll check for you.
examples.note: 'Je vais + infinitive' expresses immediate future or intention. 'Vérifier' is the verb for checking/verifying.

examples.original: Oui, voici le numéro: CB123456789FR. Selon le site, le colis est en attente de livraison.
examples.phonetic: /wi, vwasi lə nymeʁo: se be œ̃ dø tʁwa katʁ sɛ̃k sis sɛt ɥit nœf ef ɛʁ. səlɔ̃ lə sit, lə kɔli ɛ tɑ̃n atɑ̃t də livʁɛzɔ̃/
examples.translation: Yes, here is the number: CB123456789FR. According to the website, the package is awaiting delivery.
examples.note: 'En attente de livraison' is the status 'pending delivery'. 'Selon le site' = according to the tracking website.

examples.original: Il semble qu'il y ait eu un problème lors de la distribution. Je vais ouvrir une réclamation pour vous.
examples.phonetic: /il sɑ̃bl kil i ɛ y œ̃ pʁɔblɛm lɔʁ də la distʁibysjɔ̃. ʒə ve uvʁiʁ yn ʁeklamasjɔ̃ puʁ vu/
examples.translation: It seems there was a problem during distribution. I'm going to open a complaint for you.
examples.note: 'Ouvrir une réclamation' is the formal expression to start a complaint or claim. 'Lors de' means 'during' or 'at the time of'.

title: Louer un appartement / Renting an apartment
bridge: Renting an apartment in France has important particularities: the rental system is highly regulated, landlords often require a 'dossier de location' (file with documents), and there are concepts like 'caution' (deposit, usually one month's rent) and 'charges' (community fees included or not in the price). The term 'loyer' is the monthly rent, and 'état des lieux' is the inventory of the apartment's condition done upon moving in and out.
rule: Key phrases: 'Je voudrais visiter l'appartement' (I would like to visit the apartment), 'Le loyer est de combien?' (How much is the rent?), 'Les charges sont comprises?' (Are the fees included?), 'Il y a une caution?' (Is there a deposit?), 'Quand est-il disponible?' (When is it available?), 'C'est meublé ou vide?' (Is it furnished or empty?)

concept_examples.text: Je voudrais visiter l'appartement annoncé sur le site.
concept_examples.translation: I would like to visit the apartment advertised on the website.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə vudʁɛ visite lapɑʁtəmɑ̃ anɔ̃se syʁ lə sit/

concept_examples.text: Le loyer est de 850 euros, charges comprises.
concept_examples.translation: The rent is 850 euros, fees included.
concept_examples.phonetic: /lə lwaje ɛ də ɥit sɑ̃ sɛ̃kɑ̃t øʁo, ʃaʁʒ kɔ̃pʁiz/

concept_examples.text: Est-ce qu'il y a une caution à verser?
concept_examples.translation: Is there a deposit to pay?
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɛs kil i a yn kosjɔ̃ a vɛʁse/

common_error.correct_alt: Seriez-vous prêt à me louer cet appartement?
common_error.explanation: In addition to the common mistake of 'je veux' instead of 'je voudrais', one must distinguish between 'appartement' (apartment/flat) and 'maison' (detached house). In the context of French urban rentals, 'appartement' is the most common. Using the wrong term can cause confusion with the landlord.

examples.original: Bonjour, j'appelle au sujet de l'appartement à louer dans le 11ème arrondissement.
examples.phonetic: /bɔ̃ʒuʁ, ʒapɛl o syʒɛ də lapɑʁtəmɑ̃ a lwe dɑ̃ lə ɔ̃zjɛm aʁɔ̃dismɑ̃/
examples.translation: Hello, I'm calling about the apartment for rent in the 11th arrondissement.
examples.note: 'Au sujet de' (regarding/about) is a formal expression to introduce the reason for a call.

examples.original: Oui, il est toujours disponible. Vous souhaitez le visiter?
examples.phonetic: /wi, il ɛ tuʒuʁ dispɔnibl. vu swɛte lə visite/
examples.translation: Yes, it's still available. Would you like to visit it?
examples.note: 'Il est toujours disponible' — here 'toujours' means 'still', not 'always'. Context changes the meaning.

examples.original: Oui, s'il vous plaît. Est-ce que je peux venir samedi matin?
examples.phonetic: /wi, sil vu plɛ. ɛs kə ʒə pø vəniʁ samdi matɛ̃/
examples.translation: Yes, please. Can I come Saturday morning?
examples.note: 'Est-ce que je peux + infinitive?' is the standard way to ask permission politely.

examples.original: Bien sûr, disons 10h00. L'appartement fait 45 m², il est au 3ème étage avec ascenseur.
examples.phonetic: /bjɛ̃ syʁ, dizɔ̃ dizsœʁ. lapɑʁtəmɑ̃ fɛ kaʁɑ̃t sɛ̃k mɛtʁ kaʁʁe, il ɛ o tʁwazjɛm etaʒ avɛk asɑ̃sœʁ/
examples.translation: Of course, let's say 10am. The apartment is 45 m², it's on the 3rd floor with an elevator.
examples.note: 'Disons' (let's say) is used to propose a tentative time. 'Faire X m²' is the expression to indicate the surface area.

examples.original: L'appartement est meublé ou vide?
examples.phonetic: /lapɑʁtəmɑ̃ ɛ møble u vid/
examples.translation: Is the apartment furnished or empty?
examples.note: 'Meublé' (furnished) vs 'vide' (empty/unfurnished). This distinction is legally important in France: the contract and taxation vary.

examples.original: Il est vide, mais la cuisine est équipée: réfrigérateur, cuisinière et lave-vaisselle.
examples.phonetic: /il ɛ vid, mɛ la kɥizin ɛ ekipe: ʁefʁiʒeʁatœʁ, kɥizinjɛʁ e lav vɛsɛl/
examples.translation: It's empty, but the kitchen is equipped: refrigerator, stove, and dishwasher.
examples.note: 'Cuisine équipée' means a kitchen equipped with appliances. 'Cuisinière' is the stove (appliance), not the cook.

examples.original: Est-ce qu'il y a du double vitrage? Et le chauffage, comment est-il?
examples.phonetic: /ɛs kil i a dy dubl vitʁaʒ? e lə ʃofaʒ, kɔmɑ̃ ɛ til/
examples.translation: Is there double glazing? And the heating, how is it?
examples.note: 'Double vitrage' (double glazing) is important for thermal insulation. 'Chauffage' is heating; it can be individual or collective.

examples.original: Oui, il y a du double vitrage. Le chauffage est collectif au gaz, inclus dans les charges.
examples.phonetic: /wi, il i a dy dubl vitʁaʒ. lə ʃofaʒ ɛ kɔlɛktif o ɡaz, ɛ̃kly dɑ̃ le ʃaʁʒ/
examples.translation: Yes, there is double glazing. The heating is collective gas, included in the fees.
examples.note: 'Charges' includes community expenses: collective heating, elevator, cleaning of common areas, etc.

examples.original: Le loyer est de 850 euros par mois, charges comprises. Il y a une caution d'un mois de loyer.
examples.phonetic: /lə lwaje ɛ də ɥit sɑ̃ sɛ̃kɑ̃t øʁo paʁ mwa, ʃaʁʒ kɔ̃pʁiz. il i a yn kosjɔ̃ dœ̃ mwa də lwaje/
examples.translation: The rent is 850 euros per month, fees included. There is a deposit of one month's rent.
examples.note: 'Charges comprises' (CC) vs 'hors charges' (HC): important to know to compare real prices between apartments.

examples.original: Est-ce que vous avez besoin d'un dossier de location?
examples.phonetic: /ɛs kə vu zave bəzwɛ̃ dœ̃ dɔsje də lɔkasjɔ̃/
examples.translation: Do you need a rental file?
examples.note: The 'dossier de location' includes: ID, employment contract, recent pay slips, and sometimes a guarantor ('garant'). It is required in most French rentals.

examples.original: Oui, il nous faut vos trois dernières fiches de paie, votre contrat de travail et une pièce d'identité.
examples.phonetic: /wi, il nu fo vo tʁwa dɛʁnjɛʁ fiʃ də pɛ, vɔtʁ kɔ̃tʁa də tʁavaj e yn pjɛs didɑ̃tite/
examples.translation: Yes, we need your last three pay slips, your employment contract, and an ID document.
examples.note: 'Fiche de paie' is the monthly pay slip. 'Trois dernières fiches de paie' is the usual minimum requirement in France.

examples.original: D'accord. Et quand est-ce que l'appartement serait disponible?
examples.phonetic: /dakɔʁ. e kɑ̃ ɛs kə lapɑʁtəmɑ̃ səʁɛ dispɔnibl/
examples.translation: Okay. And when would the apartment be available?
examples.note: 'Serait disponible' — conditional of 'être' to ask in a softened way. Equivalent to Spanish 'estaría disponible'.

title: À une fête ou événement social / At a party or social event
bridge: At French parties and social events, introductions have their own rhythm: you give la bise (kiss on the cheek, usually two in Paris) when greeting, and there is a culture of light conversation or 'small talk' that the French handle naturally. Unlike in Spanish, the French are sometimes more reserved with strangers at first, but once the ice is broken they tend to be very open. Knowing how to introduce yourself, talk briefly about yourself, and say goodbye elegantly is key in these contexts.
rule: Key phrases: 'Je me présente, je m'appelle...' (I introduce myself, my name is...), 'Je suis venu(e) avec...' (I came with...), 'Tu connais beaucoup de monde ici?' (Do you know many people here?), 'Qu'est-ce que tu fais dans la vie?' (What do you do for a living?), 'C'était sympa de te rencontrer' (It was nice to meet you), 'Je dois y aller, bonne soirée!' (I have to go, have a good evening!)

concept_examples.text: Salut! Je ne crois pas qu'on se connaisse. Je m'appelle Sophie.
concept_examples.translation: Hi! I don't think we know each other. My name is Sophie.
concept_examples.phonetic: /saly! ʒə nə kʁwa pa kɔ̃ sə kɔnɛs. ʒə mapɛl sɔfi/

concept_examples.text: Qu'est-ce que tu fais dans la vie?
concept_examples.translation: What do you do for a living?
concept_examples.phonetic: /kɛs kə ty fɛ dɑ̃ la vi/

concept_examples.text: C'était vraiment sympa de te rencontrer ce soir!
concept_examples.translation: It was really nice to meet you tonight!
concept_examples.phonetic: /setɛ vʁɛmɑ̃ sɛ̃pa də tə ʁɑ̃kɔ̃tʁe sə swaʁ/

common_error.wrong: Je suis venu avec mon ami Marc.
common_error.correct: Je suis venu avec mon ami Marc.
common_error.correct_alt: Je suis venue avec mon amie Lucie.
common_error.explanation: The past participle 'venu' agrees in gender with the subject: a man says 'je suis venu', a woman says 'je suis venue'. This gender agreement error is very common among Spanish speakers because in Spanish the participle does not change with 'he venido'.

examples.original: Salut! Je m'appelle Marcos. Et toi?
examples.phonetic: /saly! ʒə mapɛl maʁkos. e twa/
examples.translation: Hi! My name is Marcos. And you?
examples.note: At an informal party, 'tu' is used automatically. 'Et toi?' is the most natural way to return the question.

examples.original: Moi c'est Clara. Tu es ami de Thomas?
examples.phonetic: /mwa sɛ klaʁa. ty ɛ ami də tɔma/
examples.translation: I'm Clara. Are you a friend of Thomas?
examples.note: 'Moi c'est...' is a very colloquial and natural introduction. Asking about the common host is the most typical conversation starter at parties.

examples.original: Oui, on se connaît depuis la fac. Et toi, comment tu le connais?
examples.phonetic: /wi, ɔ̃ sə kɔnɛ dəpɥi la fak. e twa, kɔmɑ̃ ty lə kɔnɛ/
examples.translation: Yes, we've known each other since university. And you, how do you know him?
examples.note: 'La fac' is the abbreviated and informal form of 'la faculté' (university). Returning the question keeps the conversation going.

examples.original: On travaille ensemble. C'est une super fête, non?
examples.phonetic: /ɔ̃ tʁavaj ɑ̃sɑ̃bl. sɛ tyn sypɛʁ fɛt, nɔ̃/
examples.translation: We work together. It's a great party, isn't it?
examples.note: 'Non?' at the end of a sentence works like 'right?' in English: it seeks confirmation or complicity.

levels.label: Parler de soi et s'intéresser à l'autre
levels.translation: Talking about yourself and showing interest in the other person

examples.original: Qu'est-ce que tu fais dans la vie?
examples.phonetic: /kɛs kə ty fɛ dɑ̃ la vi/
examples.translation: What do you do for a living?
examples.note: 'Qu'est-ce que tu fais dans la vie?' is THE French social question par excellence. It's equivalent to 'what do you do for work?' but with a broader tone.

examples.original: Je suis graphiste, je travaille en freelance. Et toi?
examples.phonetic: /ʒə sɥi ɡʁafist, ʒə tʁavaj ɑ̃ fʁilɑ̃s. e twa/
examples.translation: I'm a graphic designer, I work freelance. And you?
examples.note: 'Graphiste' means graphic designer. 'En freelance' is pronounced the same as in English and is commonly used in French.

examples.original: Moi je suis prof de maths dans un lycée à Lyon. Tu habites Paris?
examples.phonetic: /mwa ʒə sɥi pʁɔf də mat dɑ̃z œ̃ lise a ljɔ̃. ty abit paʁi/
examples.translation: I'm a math teacher at a high school in Lyon. Do you live in Paris?
examples.note: 'Prof' is the colloquial abbreviation of 'professeur'. 'Lycée' is the secondary school (equivalent to high school).

examples.original: Non, je suis de Barcelone mais je vis à Paris depuis deux ans. Tu aimes la vie ici?
examples.phonetic: /nɔ̃, ʒə sɥi də baʁsɛlɔn mɛ ʒə vi a paʁi dəpɥi dø ɑ̃. ty ɛm la vi isi/
examples.translation: No, I'm from Barcelona but I've been living in Paris for two years. Do you like life here?
examples.note: 'Je suis de...' for origin, 'je vis à...' for current residence. These are two different structures that are worth mastering.

examples.original: Bon, je crois que je vais y aller, il se fait tard. C'était vraiment sympa de parler avec toi!
examples.phonetic: /bɔ̃, ʒə kʁwa kə ʒə ve i ale, il sə fɛ taʁ. setɛ vʁɛmɑ̃ sɛ̃pa də paʁle avɛk twa/
examples.translation: Well, I think I'm going to head out, it's getting late. It was really nice talking to you!
examples.note: 'Je vais y aller' is the most natural way to announce your departure. 'Il se fait tard' = 'it's getting late'.

examples.original: Moi aussi! On devrait se revoir. Tu es sur les réseaux?
examples.phonetic: /mwa osi! ɔ̃ dəvʁɛ sə ʁəvwaʁ. ty ɛ syʁ le ʁezo/
examples.translation: Me too! We should see each other again. Are you on social media?
examples.note: 'On devrait + infinitive' (the conditional of 'devoir') expresses a friendly suggestion. 'Les réseaux' is the abbreviation of 'réseaux sociaux' (social networks).

examples.original: Oui, je suis sur Instagram. Je te donne mon pseudo: @marcos_bcn.
examples.phonetic: /wi, ʒə sɥi syʁ ɛ̃staɡʁam. ʒə tə dɔn mɔ̃ psødo: arobase maʁkos be se en/
examples.translation: Yes, I'm on Instagram. I'll give you my username: @marcos_bcn.
examples.note: 'Pseudo' (nickname/username) is the French term for the username on social media. 'Arobase' is what the @ symbol is called.

examples.original: Super! Bonne soirée et à bientôt j'espère!
examples.phonetic: /sypɛʁ! bɔn swaʁe e a bjɛ̃to ʒɛspɛʁ/
examples.translation: Great! Have a good evening and see you soon, I hope!
examples.note: 'Bonne soirée' is the standard evening farewell. 'À bientôt j'espère' adds a nuance of hope for a reunion, very polite.

translations.en: At a party or social event

title: Se plaindre et s'excuser / Complaining and Apologizing
bridge: In France, complaining has its codes: the French do not hesitate to complain when something is not right, but always with a certain formality and without losing their temper (in theory). The key term is 'se plaindre' (to complain) and 'porter réclamation' (to file a formal complaint). Apologizing also has its nuances: 'excusez-moi' is used for light apologies, while 'je suis vraiment désolé(e)' expresses more sincere regret. In shops and with neighbors, a cordial tone is essential.
rule: Key phrases: 'Je voudrais me plaindre de...' (I would like to complain about...), 'Ce n'est pas acceptable' (This is not acceptable), 'Je suis vraiment désolé(e)' (I am truly sorry), 'Ce n'est pas de ma faute' (It's not my fault), 'Pourriez-vous régler ce problème?' (Could you solve this problem?), 'Je vous présente mes excuses' (I offer you my apologies)

concept_examples.text: Je voudrais me plaindre: le produit que j'ai acheté est défectueux.
concept_examples.translation: I would like to complain: the product I bought is defective.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə vudʁɛ mə plɛ̃dʁ: lə pʁɔdɥi kə ʒe aʃte ɛ defɛktɥø/

concept_examples.text: Je suis vraiment désolé pour ce désagrément.
concept_examples.translation: I am truly sorry for this inconvenience.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə sɥi vʁɛmɑ̃ dezɔle puʁ sə dezaɡʁemɑ̃/

concept_examples.text: Pourriez-vous faire quelque chose pour résoudre ce problème?
concept_examples.translation: Could you do something to solve this problem?
concept_examples.phonetic: /puʁje vu fɛʁ kɛlkə ʃoz puʁ ʁezudʁ sə pʁɔblɛm/

common_error.correct: Il y a eu une erreur de votre côté.
common_error.correct_alt: Je pense qu'il y a eu un malentendu.
common_error.explanation: Saying 'c'est votre erreur' (it's your mistake) directly is too aggressive in French and can provoke a defensive reaction. It is much more effective and polite to use impersonal expressions like 'il y a eu une erreur de votre côté' (there has been an error on your side) or to suggest a misunderstanding with 'malentendu'. The French value indirect and civilized confrontation.

examples.original: Excusez-moi, j'ai un problème avec cet article que j'ai acheté hier.
examples.phonetic: /ɛkskyze mwa, ʒe œ̃ pʁɔblɛm avɛk sɛ taʁtikl kə ʒe aʃte jɛʁ/
examples.translation: Excuse me, I have a problem with this item I bought yesterday.
examples.note: 'Excusez-moi' at the beginning softens the complaint and makes it more receptive. It is always better to start with courtesy.

examples.original: Qu'est-ce qui ne va pas?
examples.phonetic: /kɛs ki nə va pa/
examples.translation: What is wrong?
examples.note: 'Qu'est-ce qui ne va pas?' is the standard question from the salesperson to invite you to explain the problem.

examples.original: L'appareil ne fonctionne pas correctement. Il s'arrête tout seul après cinq minutes.
examples.phonetic: /lapaʁɛj nə fɔ̃ksjɔn pa kɔʁɛktəmɑ̃. il saʁɛt tu sœl apʁɛ sɛ̃k minyt/
examples.translation: The device does not work properly. It turns off by itself after five minutes.
examples.note: 'S'arrêter tout seul' (to turn off/stop by itself) is the expression to describe spontaneous malfunction.

examples.original: Je comprends. Avez-vous votre ticket de caisse? Nous allons vous l'échanger.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə kɔ̃pʁɑ̃. ave vu vɔtʁ tikɛ də kɛs? nu zalɔ̃ vu leʃɑ̃ʒe/
examples.translation: I understand. Do you have your receipt? We will exchange it for you.
examples.note: 'Ticket de caisse' is the receipt or purchase ticket. 'Échanger' means to exchange (the product for another).

examples.original: Bonjour voisin. Je suis désolé de vous déranger, mais j'ai un problème à vous signaler.
examples.phonetic: /bɔ̃ʒuʁ vwazɛ̃. ʒə sɥi dezɔle də vu deʁɑ̃ʒe, mɛ ʒe œ̃ pʁɔblɛm a vu siɲale/
examples.translation: Hello neighbor. I am sorry to bother you, but I have a problem to report to you.
examples.note: 'Je suis désolé de vous déranger' (I am sorry to bother you) is the perfect opening to address a neighborhood conflict with tact.

examples.original: Bien sûr, dites-moi. Qu'est-ce qui se passe?
examples.phonetic: /bjɛ̃ syʁ, dit mwa. kɛs ki sə pas/
examples.translation: Of course, tell me. What is happening?
examples.note: 'Dites-moi' (tell me) is a friendly invitation to speak. 'Qu'est-ce qui se passe?' is 'What is going on?'.

examples.original: La musique chez vous est très forte le soir et cela m'empêche de dormir. Pourriez-vous baisser le volume après 22 heures?
examples.phonetic: /la myzik ʃe vu ɛ tʁɛ fɔʁt lə swaʁ e səla mɑ̃pɛʃ də dɔʁmiʁ. puʁje vu bɛse lə vɔlym apʁɛ vɛ̃t dø œʁ/
examples.translation: The music at your place is very loud in the evening and it prevents me from sleeping. Could you lower the volume after 10 PM?
examples.note: 'M'empêcher de + infinitive' = 'to prevent me from + gerund'. 'Baisser le volume' is to lower the volume. The legal quiet hours in France are usually 10 PM.

examples.original: Oh, je ne savais pas que ça vous dérangeait. Je suis vraiment désolé, je ferai attention à l'avenir.
examples.phonetic: /o, ʒə nə savɛ pa kə sa vu deʁɑ̃ʒɛ. ʒə sɥi vʁɛmɑ̃ dezɔle, ʒə fəʁɛ atɑ̃sjɔ̃ a lavniʁ/
examples.translation: Oh, I didn't know it bothered you. I am truly sorry, I will be more careful in the future.
examples.note: 'Je ne savais pas' (I didn't know) in the imperfect to explain previous ignorance. 'À l'avenir' = 'in the future / from now on'.

examples.original: Je dois vous informer que j'ai reçu ma commande avec deux semaines de retard et plusieurs articles manquants.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə dwa vu ɛ̃fɔʁme kə ʒe ʁəsy ma kɔmɑ̃d avɛk dø səmɛn də ʁətaʁ e plyzjœʁ zaʁtikl mɑ̃kɑ̃/
examples.translation: I must inform you that I received my order with two weeks of delay and several missing items.
examples.note: 'Je dois vous informer que...' is the formal opening for a written or phone complaint. 'Articles manquants' = missing items.

examples.original: Je vous présente toutes nos excuses pour ce désagrément. Cela n'aurait pas dû se produire.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə vu pʁezɑ̃t tut no zɛkskyze puʁ sə dezaɡʁemɑ̃. səla noʁɛ pa dy sə pʁɔdɥiʁ/
examples.translation: I offer you our sincere apologies for this inconvenience. This should not have happened.
examples.note: 'Cela n'aurait pas dû se produire' uses the past conditional to express that something should not have happened. It is the most standard corporate apology formula.

examples.original: Je souhaite un remboursement complet ou l'envoi des articles manquants dans les plus brefs délais.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə swɛt œ̃ ʁɑ̃buʁsmɑ̃ kɔ̃plɛ u lɑ̃vwa de zaʁtikl mɑ̃kɑ̃ dɑ̃ le ply bʁɛf delɛ/
examples.translation: I wish a full refund or the sending of the missing items as soon as possible.
examples.note: 'Dans les plus brefs délais' (as soon as possible) is the standard formal expression to demand speed in a resolution.

examples.original: Nous allons traiter votre dossier en priorité et vous contacter sous 48 heures. Encore une fois, toutes nos excuses.
examples.phonetic: /nu zalɔ̃ tʁɛte vɔtʁ dɔsje ɑ̃ pʁjɔʁite e vu kɔ̃takte su kaʁɑ̃t ɥit œʁ. ɑ̃kɔʁ yn fwa, tut no zɛkskyze/
examples.translation: We will process your file as a priority and contact you within 48 hours. Once again, our apologies.
examples.note: 'Traiter un dossier' = to process a file. 'Sous 48 heures' = within 48 hours (different from 'dans 48 heures' = in exactly 48 hours).

title: Décrire sa ville ou son village / Describing your city or village
bridge: Describing your city or village in French involves using vocabulary for location, geographical and social features, and knowing how to express both what you like and what is missing. In French, there is a clear distinction between 'ville' (city) and 'village' (village), and between 'quartier' (neighborhood) and 'banlieue' (suburb). French speakers also frequently use 'il y a' (there is/are) and 'il manque' (is missing) to describe the amenities of a place.
rule: Key phrases: 'Ma ville se trouve...' (My city is located...), 'C'est une ville/un village de [X] habitants' (It is a city/village of [X] inhabitants), 'Il y a...' (There is/are...), 'Il n'y a pas de...' (There is no...), 'Ce que j'aime, c'est...' (What I like is...), 'Ce qui manque, c'est...' (What is missing is...), 'C'est calme/animé/moderne/historique' (It is quiet/lively/modern/historic)

concept_examples.text: Ma ville se trouve dans le sud de l'Espagne, près de la mer.
concept_examples.translation: My city is located in the south of Spain, near the sea.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ma vil sə tʁuv dɑ̃ lə syd də lɛspaɲ, pʁɛ də la mɛʁ/

concept_examples.text: C'est une ville de cent mille habitants, ni trop grande ni trop petite.
concept_examples.translation: It is a city of a hundred thousand inhabitants, neither too big nor too small.
concept_examples.phonetic: /sɛ tyn vil də sɑ̃ mil abitɑ̃, ni tʁo ɡʁɑ̃d ni tʁo pətit/

concept_examples.text: Ce qui manque, c'est un bon réseau de transports en commun.
concept_examples.translation: What is missing is a good public transportation network.
concept_examples.phonetic: /sə ki mɑ̃k, sɛ œ̃ bɔ̃ ʁezo də tʁɑ̃spɔʁ ɑ̃ kɔmœ̃/

common_error.wrong: Ma ville est situé au nord.
common_error.correct: Ma ville est située au nord.
common_error.correct_alt: Ma ville se trouve au nord.
common_error.explanation: 'Situé' is a past participle adjective that agrees with the noun: 'ville' is feminine, so the correct form is 'située'. A simpler alternative is to use the pronominal verb 'se trouver' (to be located), which does not require gender agreement and is equally natural: 'ma ville se trouve au nord'.

examples.original: D'où viens-tu? Tu peux me parler de ta ville?
examples.phonetic: /du vjɛ̃ ty? ty pø mə paʁle də ta vil/
examples.translation: Where are you from? Can you tell me about your city?
examples.note: 'D'où viens-tu?' is the standard question about origin. 'Tu peux me parler de...?' invites a free description.

examples.original: Je viens de Séville, une grande ville du sud de l'Espagne. Elle est connue pour sa cathédrale et son ambiance festive.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə vjɛ̃ də sevij, yn ɡʁɑ̃d vil dy syd də lɛspaɲ. ɛl ɛ kɔny puʁ sa katedral e sɔ̃n ɑ̃bjɑ̃s fɛstiv/
examples.translation: I am from Seville, a large city in the south of Spain. It is known for its cathedral and its festive atmosphere.
examples.note: 'Elle est connue pour...' (it is known for...) is the perfect structure to highlight the most representative elements of a place.

examples.original: C'est grand comme ville?
examples.phonetic: /sɛ ɡʁɑ̃ kɔm vil/
examples.translation: Is it big as a city?
examples.note: 'C'est grand comme ville?' is a colloquial and natural question. It is equivalent to 'Is it a big city?'.

examples.original: Oui, c'est la quatrième ville d'Espagne, avec environ 700 000 habitants.
examples.phonetic: /wi, sɛ la katʁjɛm vil dɛspaɲ, avɛk ɑ̃viʁɔ̃ sɛt sɑ̃ mil abitɑ̃/
examples.translation: Yes, it is the fourth city in Spain, with about 700,000 inhabitants.
examples.note: 'Environ' (about/approximately) is the French equivalent of 'around' for approximate quantities.

examples.original: Qu'est-ce qu'il y a à faire dans ta ville?
examples.phonetic: /kɛs kil i a a fɛʁ dɑ̃ ta vil/
examples.translation: What is there to do in your city?
examples.note: 'Qu'est-ce qu'il y a à faire?' (What is there to do?) is the most natural question to ask about leisure and activities in a place.

examples.original: Il y a beaucoup de choses! Des musées, des parcs, de vieux quartiers historiques et une vie nocturne très animée.
examples.phonetic: /il i a boku də ʃoz! de myze, de paʁk, də vjø kaʁtje istɔʁik e yn vi nɔktɥʁn tʁɛ zanime/
examples.translation: There are many things! Museums, parks, old historic neighborhoods, and a very lively nightlife.
examples.note: 'Vie nocturne' (nightlife). 'Animé(e)' is a very useful adjective meaning lively/full of life, the opposite of 'calme'.

examples.original: Et le climat, c'est comment?
examples.phonetic: /e lə klima, sɛ kɔmɑ̃/
examples.translation: And the climate, how is it?
examples.note: 'C'est comment?' is the colloquial question to ask for a general description. More informal than 'How is it?'.

examples.original: Il fait très chaud en été, parfois plus de 40 degrés. En hiver, il fait doux, rarement froid.
examples.phonetic: /il fɛ tʁɛ ʃo ɑ̃n ete, paʁfwa ply də kaʁɑ̃t dəɡʁe. ɑ̃n ivɛʁ, il fɛ du, ʁaʁəmɑ̃ fʁwa/
examples.translation: It is very hot in summer, sometimes over 40 degrees. In winter, it is mild, rarely cold.
examples.note: 'Il fait doux' (it is mild/soft). 'Rarement' (rarely). Weather expressions always use 'il fait + adjective'.

levels.label: Points positifs et ce qui manque
levels.translation: Positive points and what is missing

examples.original: Qu'est-ce que tu aimes le plus dans ta ville? Et qu'est-ce qui pourrait être amélioré?
examples.phonetic: /kɛs kə ty ɛm lə ply dɑ̃ ta vil? e kɛs ki puʁɛ ɛtʁ ameljoʁe/
examples.translation: What do you like most about your city? And what could be improved?
examples.note: 'Ce qui pourrait être amélioré' uses the conditional to ask about possible improvements in a softened, non-critical way.

examples.original: Ce que j'aime le plus, c'est l'atmosphère: les gens sont chaleureux et il y a toujours quelque chose à faire.
examples.phonetic: /sə kə ʒɛm lə ply, sɛ latmɔsfɛʁ: le ʒɑ̃ sɔ̃ ʃaløʁø e il i a tuʒuʁ kɛlkə ʃoz a fɛʁ/
examples.translation: What I like most is the atmosphere: the people are warm and there is always something to do.
examples.note: 'Ce que j'aime le plus, c'est...' is the structure to highlight what you value most. 'Chaleureux' (warm/welcoming) to describe people.

examples.original: Par contre, ce qui manque vraiment, c'est un bon réseau de transports en commun. On est trop dépendant de la voiture.
examples.phonetic: /paʁ kɔ̃tʁ, sə ki mɑ̃k vʁɛmɑ̃, sɛ œ̃ bɔ̃ ʁezo də tʁɑ̃spɔʁ ɑ̃ kɔmœ̃. ɔ̃n ɛ tʁo depɑ̃dɑ̃ də la vwatyʁ/
examples.translation: On the other hand, what is really missing is a good public transportation network. We are too dependent on the car.
examples.note: 'Par contre' is the connector to introduce a contrast (equivalent to 'on the other hand / however'). 'Ce qui manque' = what is missing.

examples.original: C'est un problème fréquent dans beaucoup de villes espagnoles. Mais malgré ça, tu y retournerais vivre?
examples.phonetic: /sɛ œ̃ pʁɔblɛm fʁekɑ̃ dɑ̃ boku də vil ɛspaɲɔl. mɛ malɡʁe sa, ty i ʁətuʁnəʁɛ vivʁ/
examples.translation: That is a frequent problem in many Spanish cities. But despite that, would you go back to live there?
examples.note: 'Malgré ça' (despite that) is the concession connector. 'Tu y retournerais' uses the conditional of 'retourner' with 'y' (place pronoun = there).

title: Parler de ses loisirs / Talking about hobbies
bridge: Talking about hobbies in French requires some expressions that don't exist in Spanish. 'Faire du/de la/de l'' is used for most sports and activities ('faire du tennis', 'faire de la natation'), but 'jouer à' is used for games and team sports ('jouer au foot', 'jouer aux échecs'). To express frequency, adverbs are placed after the main verb, not at the beginning as we sometimes do in Spanish. Inviting someone to join requires the conditional: 'tu voudrais venir?' sounds much more natural than 'tu veux venir?'.
rule: Key structures: 'Je fais du/de la...' (I do/practice...), 'Je joue à...' (I play...), 'J'aime + infinitive' (I like...), 'Je vais au cinéma / au musée' (I go to the cinema / to the museum). Frequency: 'tous les jours' (every day), 'une fois par semaine' (once a week), 'de temps en temps' (from time to time), 'rarement' (rarely). Inviting: 'Tu voudrais venir avec moi?' (Would you like to come with me?), 'Ça te dit de...?' (Do you feel like...?), 'On pourrait y aller ensemble' (We could go together).

concept_examples.text: Je fais du vélo tous les week-ends.
concept_examples.translation: I go cycling every weekend.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə fɛ dy velo tu le wik ɛnd/

concept_examples.text: Ça te dit d'aller au musée samedi?
concept_examples.translation: Do you feel like going to the museum on Saturday?
concept_examples.phonetic: /sa tə di dale o myze samdi/

concept_examples.text: Je joue au foot une fois par semaine avec des collègues.
concept_examples.translation: I play football once a week with colleagues.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə ʒu o fut yn fwa paʁ səmɛn avɛk de kɔlɛɡ/

common_error.wrong: Je fais du foot avec mes amis.
common_error.correct: Je joue au foot avec mes amis.
common_error.correct_alt: Je fais de la natation / Je joue au tennis.
common_error.explanation: In French, you must distinguish between two verbs depending on the activity: 'jouer à' is used for team sports and games that have an opponent or direct game rules (football, tennis, basketball, chess). 'Faire du/de la' is used for individual activities, movement sports, or cultural activities (swimming, cycling, yoga, painting). Saying 'faire du foot' is a frequent mistake among Spanish speakers.

examples.original: Qu'est-ce que tu fais pendant ton temps libre?
examples.phonetic: /kɛs kə ty fɛ pɑ̃dɑ̃ tɔ̃ tɑ̃ libʁ/
examples.translation: What do you do in your free time?
examples.note: 'Temps libre' (free time) is the natural expression. 'Pendant' here means 'during' or 'in'.

examples.original: J'aime beaucoup lire et écouter de la musique. Et le week-end, je fais du sport.
examples.phonetic: /ʒɛm boku liʁ e ekute də la myzik. e lə wik ɛnd, ʒə fɛ dy spɔʁ/
examples.translation: I really like reading and listening to music. And on weekends, I do sports.
examples.note: 'J'aime + infinitive' is the basic structure to talk about likes. 'Faire du sport' is the general expression for 'to do sports'.

examples.original: Tu pratiques quel sport?
examples.phonetic: /ty pʁatik kɛl spɔʁ/
examples.translation: What sport do you practice?
examples.note: 'Pratiquer un sport' is the formal verb for practicing a sport. In informal conversation, you can also say 'tu fais quel sport?'.

examples.original: Je joue au basket deux fois par semaine et je fais de la natation le dimanche.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə ʒu o baskɛt dø fwa paʁ səmɛn e ʒə fɛ də la natasjɔ̃ lə dimɑ̃ʃ/
examples.translation: I play basketball twice a week and I swim on Sundays.
examples.note: Notice the difference: 'jouer au basket' (team sport) vs. 'faire de la natation' (individual activity). This distinction is fundamental in French.

examples.original: Est-ce que tu t'intéresses à l'art ou à la culture?
examples.phonetic: /ɛs kə ty tɛ̃teʁɛs a laʁ u a la kyltʁyʁ/
examples.translation: Are you interested in art or culture?
examples.note: 'S'intéresser à' (to be interested in) is a pronominal verb. The preposition is 'à', not 'por' as in Spanish, so you need to memorize it.

examples.original: Oui, je vais souvent au cinéma, environ deux fois par mois. Et toi?
examples.phonetic: /wi, ʒə ve suvɑ̃ o sinema, ɑ̃viʁɔ̃ dø fwa paʁ mwa. e twa/
examples.translation: Yes, I often go to the cinema, about twice a month. And you?
examples.note: 'Souvent' (often) always goes after the conjugated verb. 'Environ' (approximately / about) softens the number.

examples.original: Moi, je préfère les expositions. Je vais au musée de temps en temps, surtout le week-end.
examples.phonetic: /mwa, ʒə pʁefɛʁ le ɛkspɔzisjɔ̃. ʒə ve o myze də tɑ̃z ɑ̃ tɑ̃, syʁtu lə wik ɛnd/
examples.translation: I prefer exhibitions. I go to the museum from time to time, especially on weekends.
examples.note: 'De temps en temps' (from time to time) is a fixed adverbial phrase. 'Surtout' (especially) introduces the precision.

examples.original: Il y a un concert de jazz ce samedi. Tu aimes ce genre de musique?
examples.phonetic: /il i a œ̃ kɔ̃sɛʁ də dʒaz sə samdi. ty ɛm sə ʒɑ̃ʁ də myzik/
examples.translation: There's a jazz concert this Saturday. Do you like that kind of music?
examples.note: 'Ce genre de' (this kind of) is very useful for categorizing. In French, 'jazz' is masculine: 'le jazz'.

examples.original: Dis, ça te dirait d'aller voir ce film avec moi vendredi soir?
examples.phonetic: /di, sa tə diʁɛ dale vwaʁ sə film avɛk mwa vɑ̃dʁədi swaʁ/
examples.translation: Hey, would you like to go see that movie with me on Friday night?
examples.note: 'Ça te dirait de + infinitive?' (conditional) is the most natural and gentle way to propose an activity. More polite than 'tu veux?'.

examples.original: Oh, avec plaisir! C'est quel film? Je ne suis pas très au courant des sorties en ce moment.
examples.phonetic: /o, avɛk plɛziʁ! sɛ kɛl film? ʒə nə sɥi pa tʁɛz o kuʁɑ̃ de sɔʁti ɑ̃ sə mɔmɑ̃/
examples.translation: Oh, with pleasure! Which movie is it? I'm not very up to date with the releases right now.
examples.note: 'Avec plaisir' (with pleasure) is the standard enthusiastic acceptance. 'Être au courant de' (to be aware of / up to date with) is a very common expression.

examples.original: C'est le nouveau film de Cédric Klapisch. On dit que c'est excellent. La séance est à 20h, ça te convient?
examples.phonetic: /sɛ lə nuvo film də sedʁik klapiʃ. ɔ̃ di kə sɛt ɛksɛlɑ̃. la seɑ̃s ɛ a vɛ̃t œʁ, sa tə kɔ̃vjɛ̃/
examples.translation: It's the new film by Cédric Klapisch. They say it's excellent. The screening is at 8 PM, does that work for you?
examples.note: 'On dit que' (they say that) is the French equivalent of the impersonal 'they say'. 'Séance' is the movie screening. 'Ça te convient?' checks if the time works.

examples.original: Parfait, ça me convient! On se retrouve devant le cinéma un quart d'heure avant?
examples.phonetic: /paʁfɛ, sa mə kɔ̃vjɛ̃! ɔ̃ sə ʁətʁuv dəvɑ̃ lə sinema œ̃ kaʁ dœʁ avɑ̃/
examples.translation: Perfect, that works for me! Shall we meet in front of the cinema a quarter of an hour before?
examples.note: 'On se retrouve' (we meet up) is the natural way to arrange to meet in French. 'Un quart d'heure' (a quarter of an hour). 'Devant' (in front of) indicates the meeting point.

translations.en: Talking about hobbies and free time

title: Parler de ses loisirs / Talking about hobbies and free time
bridge: In Spanish we use the verb 'gustar' with an indirect object pronoun (me gusta), while in French we use 'aimer' with a subject pronoun directly (j'aime). Also note that French distinguishes between 'jouer à' for sports and games, and 'jouer de' for musical instruments, something that in Spanish is resolved with 'jugar a' and 'tocar' respectively. Another key difference: in French, 'faire de' is used for many leisure activities (faire du vélo) that in Spanish are simply expressed with the verb 'hacer' or the infinitive.
rule:
To talk about hobbies in French A2:
1. Use 'aimer' + infinitive to express general likes: J'aime lire (I like to read). Also 'adorer' (to love) and 'détester' (to hate).
2. For activities with 'jouer': use 'jouer à' + contracted article with sports and ball games (jouer au football, jouer aux échecs). Use 'jouer de' + musical instrument (jouer de la guitare, jouer du piano).
3. For activities with 'faire': use 'faire de' + contracted article (faire du vélo, faire de la natation) for many sports and leisure activities, especially with nouns.
4. Contracted articles: à + le = au, à + la = à la, à + les = aux; de + le = du, de + la = de la, de + les = des.
5. To express frequency, place adverbs like 'souvent' (often), 'parfois' (sometimes), 'rarement' (rarely) after the conjugated verb or at the beginning of the sentence.
6. In negation, use 'ne... pas' around the verb, and the indefinite or partitive article after 'pas' becomes 'de' (je ne fais pas de sport).

concept_examples.text: J'aime lire des livres.
concept_examples.translation: I like reading books.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒɛm liʁ de livʁ/

concept_examples.text: Je joue au tennis le week-end.
concept_examples.translation: I play tennis on weekends.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə ʒu o tɛnis lə wikɛnd/

concept_examples.text: Elle fait du vélo tous les matins.
concept_examples.translation: She rides a bike every morning.

concept_examples.text: Nous aimons écouter de la musique.
concept_examples.translation: We like listening to music.
concept_examples.phonetic: /nu zɛmɔ̃ ekute də la myzik/

common_error.explanation: In Spanish we say 'toco el piano' or 'juego al piano', but in French, for musical instruments we use 'jouer de', not 'jouer à'. The correct form is 'jouer du piano' (de + le). You can also use 'jouer au piano' in colloquial contexts, but 'jouer du' is more standard to indicate musical ability. Remember: 'jouer à' is for sports and games, 'jouer de' for instruments.

examples.original: J'adore la natation.
examples.phonetic: /ʒadɔʁ la natasjɔ̃/
examples.translation: I love swimming.
examples.note: Use of 'adorer' + noun to express a strong liking. In Spanish we use 'encantar' with an indirect pronoun, but here it is direct.

examples.original: Tu aimes le cinéma ?
examples.phonetic: /ty ɛm lə sinema/
examples.translation: Do you like the cinema?
examples.note: Informal question with 'tu'. Note the pronunciation of 'aimes' which sounds like /ɛm/.

examples.original: Je déteste le shopping.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə detɛst lə ʃɔpiŋ/
examples.translation: I hate shopping.
examples.note: Use of 'détester' + noun. In France, 'shopping' is used as a loanword from English.

examples.original: Je joue au football avec mes amis.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə ʒu o futbol avɛk me zami/
examples.translation: I play football with my friends.
examples.note: Use of 'jouer à' with sports: 'au' = à + le. Do not confuse with 'je fais du football' (less common).

examples.original: Elle joue aux échecs.
examples.phonetic: /ɛl ʒu o zɛʃɛk/
examples.translation: She plays chess.
examples.note: Note: 'aux' = à + les, because 'échecs' is plural. In Spanish we say 'jugar al ajedrez', but in French it is plural.

examples.original: Nous faisons du sport tous les jours.
examples.phonetic: /nu fəzɔ̃ dy spɔʁ tu le ʒuʁ/
examples.translation: We do sports every day.
examples.note: Use of 'faire de' + noun. 'Faire du sport' is a common expression for exercise.

examples.original: Je vais souvent à la piscine.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə vɛ suvɑ̃ a la pisɛ̃/
examples.translation: I often go to the pool.
examples.note: The adverb 'souvent' is placed after the conjugated verb. In Spanish, 'a menudo' usually goes at the end.

examples.original: Elle écoute parfois de la musique.
examples.phonetic: /ɛl ekut paʁfwa də la myzik/
examples.translation: She sometimes listens to music.
examples.note: Adverb 'parfois' in the middle of the sentence. In Spanish, 'a veces' can vary in position.

examples.original: Je ne joue jamais aux jeux vidéo.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə ʒu ʒamɛ o ʒø vido/
examples.translation: I never play video games.
examples.note: Use of 'ne... jamais' to express 'never'. The adverb goes after the verb. Note the negation with 'ne' elided to 'n'' before a vowel.

translations.en: Talking about hobbies and free time
